correctness.rationale: Each projective generator-column multiplicity m(P) determines the weight N-m(P) on its annihilator message line. The q+1 line weights recover nonzero length by summing to qN. PGL2(2)=S3 and PGL2(3)=S4; PGL2(4)=A5 by parity of generators and group order 60. Distinct quaternary multiplicities need at least 10 positions. At t>=0 the prescribed multiplicities are distinct, target differs by an odd transposition, and all allowed weight-ratio permutations are odd. Any nontrivial permutation of five consecutive descending weights has maximum ratio at least (4t+10)/(4t+9) and minimum at most its reciprocal; the direct basis map attains both. Exact GF4 codeword and GL2 enumeration independently returned VERIFY_OK for six t values, but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 code distortion metric quantifies the difference between linear codes beyond code-equivalence yes/no. The new theorem pins down the first q and shortest n where a complete Hamming spectrum fails as a code equivalence invariant in dimension two, and computes a sharp positive distance gap that tends to 1 over an infinite explicit family. This creates a natural stability boundary for code distortion under the strict linear category, with a meaningful contrasting semilinear boundary. The result is not merely a finite table; it has an unbounded parameter law and exact optimal mapping argument.
